title: github-backup(fetch): a missing mirror can never trip the chronic alarm — 'missing' returns before any fail_days record, so the daily run exits 0 forever

body:
## Problem

In the daily fetch (`infra/github-backup/bin/fetch_mirrors.py`), a planned mirror that is **missing on disk can never trip the chronic-failure alarm**: every daily run reports it, writes a `fetch.log` line, and exits 0 — forever. A repo whose `git fetch` *fails* exits 1 on its third failure day; a repo with no mirror at all is structurally invisible to that mechanism, even though it is the worse state (there is no backup to be stale).

## Evidence (verified this run on main `e08fceb4`)

- `fetch_mirrors.py:22-23` — `fetch_repo` returns `"missing"` when `valid_mirror(path)` is false, **before** the `state.setdefault(repo, {})` at line 28 and before any `fail_days` recording (lines 34-37, failure path only).
- `fetch_mirrors.py:72-75` — the run's only non-zero exit path is `chronic = [repos with len(fail_days) >= 3]`; a missing repo never accumulates `fail_days`, so `chronic` can never contain it. The docstring (lines 5-7) states the exit code exists "so systemd shows the failure" — the oneshot `github-backup-fetch.service` has no other failure signal.
- The weekly reconcile does re-clone missing mirrors, but if the mirror disappears again (or the clone pass fails), the daily fetch — the only daily signal — stays green indefinitely; MANIFEST.json says `missing` but nothing reads it as an alarm.

### Probe (laptop, verbatim copies, sha256-matched)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-fetchmissing/` (laptop) — `fetch_mirrors.py` / `ghb_common.py` / `manifest.py` sha256-identical to sandbox main `e08fceb4`; fake HOME with a two-repo `plan.json`:

```text
RUN 1 (missing repo + control repo whose remote is a nonexistent local path, seeded with 2 prior fail_days):
{"results": {"ok": 0, "fail": 1, "skip": 0, "missing": 1}, "chronic_failures": ["owner/failing-one"]}  exit=1
MANIFEST: {'owner/failing-one': 'mirrored', 'owner/missing-one': 'missing'}
RUNS 2-4 (missing repo alone, three more daily passes):
{"results": {"ok": 0, "fail": 0, "skip": 0, "missing": 1}, "chronic_failures": []}  exit=0   (x3)
state.json after all runs: no entry for owner/missing-one at all — fail_days is never created for it.
```

The control proves the chronic mechanism works for fetch *failures*; the missing path bypasses it entirely.

## Why it matters

The mirror set is the disaster-recovery source for the whole estate (see `infra/github-backup/README.md`). A mirror deleted, corrupted past `valid_mirror`, or never cloned after a plan change is exactly the loss the daily fetch exists to surface — and it is the one outcome its alarm cannot express. The failure is silent in the only channel systemd watches (the exit code).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A repo reported `missing` by the daily pass is recorded in state (e.g. its own missing-days list, or `fail_days`) so repeated daily misses eventually make the run exit non-zero, on the same 3-day scale as fetch failures — or a single missing mirror exits non-zero immediately, with the choice recorded in triage.
- [ ] A transient/one-day missing state that the weekly reconcile repairs does not latch the alarm after the mirror returns (state for the repo clears on the next `ok`, as `fail_days` does at line 31).
- [ ] Regression coverage (script-level test or probe script checked in): missing-on-3-days run exits 1; control fetch-failure behaviour unchanged; a repo that returns to `ok` clears its record.
- [ ] Distinct from #3219 (drainer acking webhook events for missing mirrors) and #3257 (fail_days counting non-consecutive days): this issue is only the daily fetch pass's missing path never reaching the exit code.

## Dedup

Checked open + recently closed github-backup issues this run: #3215 (umbrella), #3219 (drain ack on failed/missing fetch), #3229 (null owner), #3233 (partial clone), #3238 (bare-skeleton valid_mirror), #3240 (non-atomic state writes), #3250 (fetch timeout), #3257 (fail_days consecutiveness). None covers the daily pass's missing-mirror exit code.
